newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Deutsche Bank prices A$300 mln note issue.
newsitem.headline: Deutsche Bank prices A$300 mln note issue.

text.p: Deutsche Bank AG said on Monday its principle subordinated extendible notes issue was priced a day ahead of schedule due to investor demand, with the issue size being increased to AS$300 million from A$250 million.

Both floating and fixed rate notes were issued. The floating rate tranche of A$250 million was issued at 23 basis points over BBSW, while the A$50 million fixed rate tranche, carrying an 8.0 percent coupon, went at a yield of 8.085 percent, Deutsche said.
"The pricing is consistent with prevailing pricing for Deutsche Bank group subordinated debt in the U.S. markets," Deutsche said in a statement.

"The issue has been purchased by a wide range of investors, and managers to the issue expect that there will be residual demand in the secondary market," group treasurer Chum Darvall said, adding some allocations to investors had to be reduced.
The bank said proceeds will be used as a capital hedge for the group in Australia and will support general working capital needs.
